GEOMETRY — subordinate only to the product invariants.
Use Image 1 for the product's exact appearance, view and pixel size; the active density branch determines whether its x-y position is fixed or may translate. Apply the product-placement and recomposed-support policy below.
ACTIVE BRANCH: LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE. Choose product x-y freely for usable composition using rigid image-plane translation only; movement is optional. Preserve exact pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never resize, reorient, reproject, or crop the product. Use LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE placement: translate the laptop rigidly to the right-hand workstation, keeping its current vertical level and leaving roughly half a laptop-width between its rightmost point and the frame. Preserve its exact pixel dimensions and all other product geometry. Independently build a sturdy rectangular worktable beneath it, with a pale oak top and charcoal metal legs. Its left end sits inside the frame, leaving a broad floor aisle along the left glass wall. Clear tabletop extends about one laptop-width to the laptop's left, with generous clearance behind and adequate clearance on the right. The whole base rests naturally on the top near the user-facing edge. Place the working chair directly in line with the keyboard on the near side, pulled back below the product silhouette and cropped at the bottom.

Camera: Keep the laptop's existing near-frontal, gently elevated view, showing its screen, keyboard and front chassis without changing their perspective. Use a low seated-eye-height camera looking gently downward, with no roll and a natural moderately wide room view. Build the tabletop's long edges rising gently toward image right and its depth edges receding toward the upper left, with coherent shared vanishing geometry throughout the glass walls, table and floor. The near edge remains close enough for keyboard access; the chair stands beyond that edge, not on an extension of the tabletop.

Composition: The fully visible laptop occupies the middle-right at its original vertical level. The pale oak worktable occupies the middle plane, with an empty work area to the laptop's left and a broad unobstructed floor aisle farther left. Its whole base is supported with natural contact shadow, clear side and rear margins, and a small reach gap at the near working edge. A charcoal upholstered working chair occupies the near-right plane, aligned directly with the keyboard, pulled back and bottom-cropped so its back remains below the laptop. A broad slate blue felt privacy screen stands on the floor in the far background, center-right, with a substantial uninterrupted panel visible above the table. Clear glass walls with slender dark mullions enclose the far and left sides. Cool even daylight enters from the left with generous fill and gentle reflections. No requested object is omitted; chair cropping preserves both direct working alignment and complete product visibility. Only rigid product translation is permitted, while support and room are independently recomposed.

TRANSLATION-ONLY PRODUCT PLACEMENT; RECOMPOSED SUPPORT
Determine density from the existing product guide bounds on the current canvas. HIGH-FILL/CLOSE applies when product width or height is at least 45% of the corresponding canvas dimension. LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE applies only when both are below 45%.

In both branches, preserve product identity, exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, projection, perspective, foreshortening, silhouette proportions, state, finish, details, logo, display content and full visibility.

HIGH-FILL/CLOSE: Preserve the product's exact initial x-y coordinates from the supplied guide. This is unconditional: do not test relocation feasibility and do not move the product even if exact size and all other invariants could be preserved. Drop any user relocation, centering, layout, emphasis, support-edge or composition request that conflicts with this fixed product position. Independently recompose support and room around the fixed product.

LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE: Choose product x-y freely for usable composition using rigid image-plane translation only; movement is optional. Independently recompose support and room beneath or around the product; product and support need not move together. Preserve every product invariant. Do not move the product merely to center it or make it more prominent.

Preserve exact product pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never shrink, enlarge, zoom, reframe, rotate, reproject, or crop the product to make a move feasible. Support axes, room perspective, horizon and vanishing geometry must be compatible with the unchanged product projection at its chosen position; do not retain incompatible geometry from the initial layout.

Keep exactly one product, entirely inside the frame and fully visible. No prop, furniture edge or foreground object may occlude it. Remove the gray guide, diagram marks and any ghost or duplicate product. If the product moves, complete the vacated location as part of the scene. If a candidate placement violates any product or support requirement, choose another placement or recompose the support and room without relaxing the product invariants.
